chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-'Abbas ibn Ma'ruf from Safwan ibn Yahya from 'Abdullah ibn Muskān and Muhammad ibn al-Nu'man al-Aḥwal from Abū 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"When a traveler joins a group of residents in their prayer, if it is the first prayer (Dhuhr), he should make the obligatory prayer in the first two rak'ahs; and if it is 'Asr, he should make the first two rak'ahs voluntary (nafl) and the last two obligatory." The jurisprudence of this hadith is that he said 'if it is Dhuhr' because whenever he does that, it is permissible for him to make the last two rak'ahs the prayer of 'Asr. And if it is the prayer of 'Asr, he only makes the last two rak'ahs his prayer because it is disliked to pray after the 'Asr prayer except in the manner of Qada (making up). And whoever prays as we mentioned, nothing remains upon him, and he counts it among the voluntary prayers.

Al-Shaykh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: "And the one who performs tayammum does not lead those who perform wudu, and the one who performs wudu does not lead those who perform tayammum." This issue is like the first one in that it is preferable that the one who performs tayammum does not lead those who perform wudu. And if he does that, it does not invalidate his prayer, but he has left the more preferable option. As for that which indicates the dislike of that, it is what we narrated:
ai.seo_question: How should a traveler combine prayers when joining a congregation of residents?
ai.summary: This ruling from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* addresses the practical flexibility for travelers joining congregational prayers, ensuring they fulfill obligations without incurring the makruh of praying after 'Asr. It further clarifies the hierarchy of leadership in prayer, noting that while a mutayammim (one performing dry ablution) leading mutawaddi'in (those with water ablution) is valid, it is considered less optimal (afdal) to maintain ritual purity consistency.
